title: In Time of Test, Family Is Best
description: Family life and relationships: the four roles that hold a family together and the line between an instrumental role (money, food, shelter, decisions, discipline) and an affective one (comfort, warmth, reassurance); the structure If + present + present for an automatic or habitual result; want + object + to-infinitive for what one person wishes another would do; the causatives make, let and have + object + base form for forcing, allowing and arranging; word building on the vocabulary of roles and feelings (the suffixes -ful, -less, -ly and the reversing prefixes un-, im-, in-, dis-, mis-); the silent letters and the consonant and vowel sounds of the module; and the language of the generation gap — complaining, interrupting, disagreeing politely, giving an opinion, with the idioms see eye to eye, get in someone's hair, blow a problem out of proportion and feel like a puppet
